title: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit High
plain: The computer sees a signal or voltage in the shift solenoid C circuit that is higher than it should be. The shift solenoid opens and closes oil passages so the transmission can change gears.
symptoms: Transmission may stay in one gear (limp mode)

causes.name: Open or broken wire in the shift solenoid circuit
Wire shorted to another power circuit

checks: Check the connector for pushed-out or loose pins
Check the shift solenoid circuit for an open wire or a short to voltage
Test the shift solenoid against the factory specification
fix: Repair the open or shorted wire or bad connector; if the wiring is good, replace the shift solenoid.

title: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The shift solenoid D is giving readings that don't match what the computer expects for the current conditions. The shift solenoid opens and closes oil passages so the transmission can change gears.
symptoms: Transmission may stay in one gear (limp mode)

causes.name: Low, dirty or wrong-type transmission fluid
Sticking valve in the valve body
High resistance in the wiring or connector
Control module software needs an update

checks: Check the transmission fluid level and condition
Compare the shift solenoid reading with what it should be on a scan tool
Inspect the wiring and connector for corrosion or damage
fix: Correct any fluid or wiring problem first; if the readings are still wrong, replace the shift solenoid.

title: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees a signal or voltage in the shift solenoid D circuit that is lower than it should be. The shift solenoid opens and closes oil passages so the transmission can change gears.
symptoms: Transmission may stay in one gear (limp mode)

causes.name: Wire shorted to ground in the shift solenoid circuit

checks: Inspect the shift solenoid wiring for chafed spots touching metal
Check the circuit for a short to ground with a meter
Unplug the shift solenoid and see whether the reading changes
fix: Fix any shorted or damaged wiring; if the wiring is good, replace the shift solenoid.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit for the transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch E, which reports hydraulic pressure (or on some transmissions, the selected gear range) to the transmission computer.
symptoms: Transmission may stay in one gear (limp mode)

causes.name: Broken or damaged wiring to the pressure sensor/switch
Blown fuse or missing power or ground

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the pressure sensor/switch for damage, rubbing or corrosion
Check related fuses, power and ground with a meter
Test the pressure sensor/switch against the factory specification before replacing it
fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the pressure sensor/switch.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Intermittent
plain: The signal from the transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch E keeps dropping out or jumping around, which usually points to a loose connection or a damaged wire.
symptoms: Transmission may stay in one gear (limp mode)
Problem may come and go, often over bumps

causes.name: Chafed wiring that opens or shorts as it moves

checks: Wiggle-test the wiring and connector while watching live data
Look for rubbed-through wiring near brackets and moving parts
fix: Repair the loose connection or damaged wire; replace the pressure sensor/switch only if it fails testing.
